and disclosed) and independently re-confirmed by reading the actual policy PDFs in docs/.

actual PDF text in docs/, cited in each case's rationale.

cases.summary:
Claim: 26-9800992
Date of Loss: April 7, 2026  
Policy & Edition: HO-0500 Edition 01-23 – identifier does not appear in the retrieved material; retrieved forms: HO-0304 (editions 01-22, 02-23) and Endorsement HO-2306  
Loss Description: The sump pump motor burned out, causing the sump to overflow into the finished basement.  
Coverage Determination: Pay up to $5,000 (limit of endorsement); excess amount denied.  
Basis: Endorsement HO-2306 – “Subject to the limit shown below, we cover direct physical loss caused by water or waterborne material which backs up through sewers or drains, or which overflows or is discharged from a sump, sump pump, or related equipment… LIMIT OF LIABILITY $5,000 per occurrence.” (Endorsement HO-2306, attached to Form HO-0304, Edition 01-22 or 02-23)  
Deductible: not stated

gold_answer.call: deny -- water/waterborne overflow from a sump falls under F-3 Water Backup; even if paid, no endorsement can buy it back here (see must_not_cite)
must_not_cite: Endorsement HO-2306 as attachable to HO-0500 -- HO-2306's own CONDITIONS text limits it to HO-0304, Edition 01-22 or 02-23
gold_answer.rationale: The notes name HO-0500 Edition 01-23, but no HO-0500 chunk was ever retrieved for this trace (confirmed from retrieval.hits) -- the top 5 hits are all HO-0304/HO-2306. HO-0500's own F-3 Water Backup exclusion (docs/HO-0500_ed-01-23.pdf) excludes 'loss caused by water that backs up through sewers or drains, or that overflows from a sump' unless the Section II peril 'accidental discharge from within a plumbing system' applies -- a sump motor burnout is a mechanical failure, not that peril, so F-3 applies and the loss is denied. Separately, Endorsement HO-2306 (docs/Endorsement_HO-2306.pdf) states in its own CONDITIONS that it 'applies only while attached to Form HO-0304, Edition 01-22 or Edition 02-23' -- it cannot be on an HO-0500 policy at all, so even if the adjuster believes it's attached, there is no valid buy-back available.

gold_answer.call: deny -- theft of building materials from a dwelling under construction is excluded until the dwelling is completed and occupied
must_not_cite: Coverage C (personal property) as the governing provision -- building materials for an unfinished addition are not the insured's personal property in the sense Coverage C covers, and E-19 governs this fact pattern specifically
gold_answer.rationale: docs/HO-0304_ed-01-22.pdf, Section III: 'E-19 Theft in Course of Construction. We do not cover theft of building materials from a dwelling under construction until the dwelling is completed and occupied.' This is a direct, on-point match for lumber and windows stolen from an addition that is still under construction. The summary paid the claim under Coverage C, stating no applicable exclusion appears in this edition -- E-19 does appear in this edition's Section III, it simply was not retrieved for this trace.
